canonical_question: Why did the Ni 25 Co 25 Cr 25 Fe 25 alloy show the highest number of worn atoms compared to the Ni 25 Co 25 Cr 30 Fe 20 alloy?

question_variants.question: Why did the Ni 25 Co 25 Cr 25 Fe 25 alloy show the highest number of worn atoms compared to the Ni 25 Co 25 Cr 30 Fe 20 alloy?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided evidence states the observation that Ni25Co25Cr25Fe25 had the highest number of worn atoms while Ni25Co25Cr30Fe20 had the lowest, but does not provide the specific mechanistic rationale (e.g., dislocation density, composition effect) for why the 25Fe variant wore more than the 30Cr variant in the context of the provided snippets.

answers.answer: The text states the finding that the Ni 25 Co 25 Cr 25 Fe 25 high entropy alloy had the highest number of worn atoms, while the Ni 25 Co 25 Cr 30 Fe 20 high entropy alloy had the lowest number, and links increased dislocations with Co content increases. However, it does not explicitly explain the specific mechanism causing the Ni25Co25Cr25Fe25 to wear more than the Ni25Co25Cr30Fe20 alloy beyond the observation of dislocation trends with Co.
answers.material: Ni 25 Co 25 Cr 25 Fe 25 and Ni 25 Co 25 Cr 30 Fe 20 high entropy alloys
answers.measurement_outcome: Ni 25 Co 25 Cr 25 Fe 25 had the highest number of worn atoms; Ni 25 Co 25 Cr 30 Fe 20 had the lowest
answers.mechanism: Dislocations increased with the increase of Co content (general trend noted)
answers.boundary_limitation: Specific rationale for the difference between 25Fe and 30Cr variants not detailed in snippet
evidence_spans: Li et al. [ [26] ] found that FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on the surface of a Cu matrix can effectively improve the wear resistance of the material by the molecular dynamics method.

They reached the conclusion that an increase of the friction velocity results in the reduction of the tangential force affected by material thermal softening and the increase of the normal force affected by material strain rate hardening, and therefore leads to the reduction of the friction coefficient [ [26] ].

In the interface area between the high entropy alloy coating and the Al substrate, due to the laser heating during the manufacturing process of the high entropy alloy coating, a part of the substrate melts and reacts with other elements in the coating forming several BCC structures which can effectively protect the matrix material from wear. [ [27] ].
